Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 32.51% while its revenue rose by 9.46% over the past year. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranks ninth for earnings growth and sixth for revenue growth. [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] led the sector in earnings expansion, and [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] delivered the strongest revenue increase. In Singapore, the sector’s performance was bolstered by strong domestic demand for staple food items, stable food‑price inflation and continued consumption of essential household products, which together create a uniquely resilient market environment for non‑cyclical consumer firms.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector posted a modest decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of negative 3.48 percent, while revenue expanded by 15.8 percent. Among fifteen sectors, it ranks twelfth for earnings growth but leads the pack in revenue growth, securing the top position. [#51O.SI]MSM International Ltd[\#51O.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase in the sector, and [#5OX.SI]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX.SI] recorded the highest revenue surge. Growth in Singapore’s Consumer Cyclicals is closely tied to seasonal tourism that lifts retail and hospitality sales, and to rising household disposable income driven by wage gains in service industries. At the same time, tighter personal loan credit conditions have restrained spending on big‑ticket items, influencing earnings performance.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector posted modest earnings growth of 1.2% and revenue growth of 2.71% over the past year. It ranks 11th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth and also 11th for revenue growth. Within the sector, [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion, while [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] led revenue growth. Growth is shaped by Singapore’s ongoing port expansion, tighter emission regulations for freight operators, and the surge in e‑commerce deliveries that strain last‑mile networks.
Healthcare: Healthcare posted a sharp decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of negative 78.64%, placing the sector 14th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth. Revenue, however, expanded by 13.11% on average, giving the sector the fourth best rank among all sectors for revenue growth. The strongest earnings performer was [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase in the group, while [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] led the sector in revenue expansion. Growth in Singapore’s healthcare market is shaped by tighter regulatory scrutiny on medical product approvals and a rapidly aging population that drives demand for specialised services, factors that uniquely influence the sector’s performance. Despite the earnings contraction, the revenue momentum reflects these structural drivers.
Properties & Real Estate: Over the past year the Properties & Real Estate sector posted an average earnings growth of about 82.6%, placing it third among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the sector rose by roughly 14.7%, also earning a third-place ranking for revenue growth. The strongest performer was [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI], which led the sector in both earnings and revenue growth. Growth has been amplified by Singapore’s constrained land supply and the government’s ongoing push for higher‑density residential projects, which together drive demand for redevelopment and new construction. At the same time, tighter regulations on foreign property purchases have reshaped market dynamics, further influencing the sector’s performance.
Energy: The Energy sector posted a contraction in earnings, with an average annual earnings decline of 8.59%, while revenue grew only modestly at 0.36% over the past year. This performance placed the sector 13th out of 15 for earnings growth and 14th out of 15 for revenue growth, indicating weak relative momentum. [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings growth within the sector, and [#BDU.SI]Federal International (2000) Ltd[\#BDU.SI] recorded the highest yearly revenue growth. Unique to Singapore, the sector is constrained by the country’s reliance on imported crude oil, regulatory caps on power generation capacity, and a policy shift toward renewable energy that limits traditional fossil‑fuel profit margins while offering limited new revenue streams.
Utilities: Despite a sharp contraction in revenue, the Utilities sector posted an average earnings increase of about 50.11% over the past year, placing it fifth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. The sector’s revenue fell by roughly 5.68%, the lowest performance ranking of all sectors at fifteenth place. [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI] led the group with the strongest yearly earnings expansion, while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] delivered the best revenue growth within the sector. In Singapore, utilities are heavily influenced by the nation’s stringent grid reliability standards and ongoing government initiatives to expand renewable energy capacity, which can boost profitability but also require substantial capital outlays that pressure revenue streams. These market‑specific dynamics help explain the divergence between robust earnings and declining revenue.
Consumer Defensive: Over the past year the Consumer Defensive sector delivered an average earnings growth of 52.84%, placing it fourth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the sector grew at an average annual rate of 10.93%, which ranks it fifth for revenue growth. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] led the sector with the strongest yearly earnings increase, while [#5EG.SI]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG.SI] posted the highest revenue growth. Growth has been reinforced by Singapore’s strong demand for essential services such as education and locally produced food, as well as government initiatives that support food security and encourage household spending on staple goods. These sector‑specific dynamics helped sustain the robust earnings surge despite broader market fluctuations.
Financial Services: Over the past year the Financial Services sector posted an average earnings growth of 8.94% and an average revenue growth of 8.82%. This places the sector tenth in earnings growth and eighth in revenue growth among the fifteen SGX sectors. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion in the group, while [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. The sector’s performance is further shaped by Singapore’s robust regulatory framework that encourages capital market development and by the city‑state’s high savings rate, which fuels demand for wealth‑management and insurance products. In addition, rapid adoption of digital banking platforms and a supportive fintech ecosystem have helped drive both earnings and revenue gains.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted an average annual earnings decline of about 123.39% while its revenue grew modestly by roughly 2.99% over the past year. This performance placed the sector at the bottom of the earnings growth ranking, 15th out of 15 sectors, and in the lower half for revenue growth, ranking 10th. Within the sector, [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] delivered the strongest gains, leading both earnings and revenue growth among its peers. The sector’s results are shaped by Singapore’s stringent content licensing rules, which can limit the speed at which new services launch. Additionally, the high cost of acquiring broadcast spectrum and the competitive pressure from established telecom operators compress margins for service providers. These market‑specific dynamics help explain why earnings fell sharply even as top line revenue showed modest improvement.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 1253.96 percent, ranking first in earnings growth among fifteen sectors. Its average annual revenue grew by 9.18 percent, which placed the sector seventh in revenue growth. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] recorded the highest earnings expansion in the sector, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] achieved the strongest revenue increase. In Singapore, a surge in infrastructure spending and tighter local regulations that favour domestic producers of construction inputs have amplified earnings momentum for basic material firms. At the same time, modest export demand for specialty chemicals supports the sector’s more measured revenue growth.
Infrastructures: Despite modest revenue expansion, the Infrastructures sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with average annual earnings growth of roughly 342 percent, placing it second among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. Revenue rose only about 1.8 percent on average, which ranks the sector thirteenth for revenue growth. The sector’s earnings boost is driven by large‑scale public infrastructure projects and the rollout of next‑generation telecommunications networks, both of which create high‑margin contracts for service providers. [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings increase, while [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] recorded the top revenue growth within the sector. These dynamics reflect the sector’s reliance on government‑led capital programmes and the unique demand for connectivity and aircraft maintenance services in Singapore.
REIT: Over the past year the REIT sector posted an average earnings growth of 37.43%, placing it eighth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a more modest 4.13% on average, which ranks the sector ninth for revenue growth. The strong earnings surge is driven in part by Singapore’s limited land supply and the government’s continued support for real estate development, which pushes rental yields higher. Meanwhile, tighter financing conditions and the gradual recovery of tourism and office demand temper revenue gains. Within the sector, [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] delivered the fastest earnings increase, while [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] led the group in revenue growth. These dynamics illustrate how sector‑specific factors such as property scarcity and evolving tenant mix shape the REIT performance in Singapore.
Industrials: The Industrials sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 45.57%, which places it sixth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. At the same time, average annual revenue grew by 2.3%, ranking the sector twelfth for revenue growth. [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth in the sector, while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] recorded the strongest revenue increase. Growth in this segment is further shaped by Singapore’s ongoing port capacity upgrades and the government’s push for smart‑factory and renewable‑energy projects, which create specific demand for industrial equipment and services.
Technology: The Technology sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 40.5%, placing it seventh among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at an average annual rate of roughly 15.2%, which ranks the sector second for revenue growth. Within the sector, [#BLU.SI]GRP Ltd[\#BLU.SI] recorded the strongest yearly earnings increase, while [#9MT.SI]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT.SI] led the market in revenue growth. The sector’s momentum is reinforced by Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives, generous R&D tax incentives and the island’s role as a regional data-center hub, all of which uniquely support technology firms.
